Hello everyone!


I bought a new Samsung Galaxy tablet and it arrived a few days ago. I needed a new note taking tablet for school. I was using my ipad before but I hate using it and I was running out of storage. I can't even upgrade the storage on there. There was no way I was gonna try to give up my left kidney for a new ipad so I went with finding an inexpensive android tablet to use that was compatible with LineageOS. 


I made a youtube video talking about it.



Right now I'm trying to transfer all of my notes and note materials over to my Samsung tablet. I'm also trying to download some of lecture videos from my previous classes onto it as well. I wish canvas has like a download video button or something cuz I has to search for extensions that would work. The extensions wouldn't work properly on the browsers that support extensions so I has to use my laptop. Good thing an app called LocalSend exists cuz I was not in the mood to fiddle around with the cords right now.


As I mentioned in the video, drawing on it works well. I had no issues with the s pen. The palm rejection isn't great though so you will need to wear two artists gloves on one hand or if you are like me who hates wearing gloves, use a thick wash cloth to be a barrier between your hand and the screen. I'm not gonna using this tablet for drawing though but if my Doogee tablet spontaneously combusts then this would be a good substitute.


I did need to install some google apps back on the devices using MindTheGApps because there are apps I need for school. I don't like how it had to be installed on the system level though. I wish Lineage had the same sandboxing feature that GraphineOS has with Google Play Services. I'm looking to see if its possible with LineageOS. Found some forums where some people tried doing it but their projects were abandoned. I won't give up though. If I figure it out, I'll make a blog post about it.


I recommend trying to find tech (or anything really) second hand or look to other sites instead of buying from Amazon or other major greedy companies if you can. I was able to save a lot of money that way. Also depending on what tech you are buying, you don't have to get the newest ones. Most of it nowadays is overpriced for what they offer and is riddled with ai bull shit and is a surveillance machine. Try an see if you can find devices that don't have ai that works well (Hopefully the ones that were released before the ai craze are still out there), or see if you can remove or hide the ai features in any way. And if you find a device you like, try looking into the settings to and enabling and disabling features for the most privacy you can get. For me, if I'm going to buy any new android tablets, I want to see if I can install a custom rom on them to de-google them and if I get a new laptop, Linux is gonna be installed. I would like to install Linux on my current laptop but I don't wanna lose and break anything. I want to get a new one, install Linux on that one, transfer what I can over, and then install Linux on my current one.


I hope my video and this blog post was helpful to those looking for a new android tablet to use but don't want the original OS on it. Hope you all have a good rest of your timezone!
